b.text: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 51% YoY to INR 1,263 million, supported by 46% growth in items ordered; normalized EBITDA increased 50% and normalized PAT 71%.
Demand indicators included 60% organic traffic, nearly 50% repeat behavior, and purchase displacement of INR 4,136 million, up 52% YoY.
Growth was delivered alongside normalized EBITDA margin of 41%, normalized EBIT margin of 23%, and normalized ROCE of ~26%.
Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 1,263 million, up 51% YoY and 15% QoQ; total income rose 49.8% YoY.
Normalized EBITDA was INR 523 million, up from INR 348 million YoY; normalized EBIT was INR 293 million, up from INR 194 million.
Normalized PAT reached INR 219 million, up from INR 128 million YoY; normalized PAT margin rose from 15% to 17.3%.
Reported EBITDA was reduced by an INR 113.7 million one-time Noida warehouse fire loss; reported EBITDA was ~INR 41 crore versus normalized EBITDA of ~INR 52 crore.
Cash flow from operations grew 49.6% YoY; FY26 operating cash flow of ~INR 173 crore broadly covered INR 87.5 crore growth CapEx.
Management expects historical demand trends to remain supportive, citing rising keyword volumes and Q1 growth, while declining to set specific forward growth expectations.
City expansion remains on the roadmap; Indore and Lucknow were cited as fast-growing markets, with expansion viewed as both a growth and customer-experience lever.
Management said supply does not constrain growth; operating cash flow, CapEx funding, and borrowing capacity provide room to pursue growth.
Revenue is cumulative, with deployed assets generating revenue for the following 18 months; management recommends assessing performance YoY due to seasonal revenue and profit patterns.
Experience-store count reached 89 from 82 in March; all stores are company-operated, and offline grew 83% YoY.
Organic traffic represented 60% of total traffic; paid traffic was ~30% excluding referrals, while offline was an increasingly important acquisition channel.
Items ordered were 329,159, up 46% YoY and 27% QoQ; live subscribers rose 36% and live items 41% YoY.
Occupancy was reported at 85%–86% for the quarter; management described 83%–84% as its preferred inventory-planning range.
Normalized EBITDA margin held at 41% and normalized EBIT margin at ~23%; normalized PAT margin increased to 17.3% from 15%.
Normalized ROE was ~27%–28% and normalized ROCE ~26%; normalized ROE was also cited at ~28%, up 198 bps YoY.
Weighted average cost of debt was ~9.58%; latest borrowing cost was 8.95%, and FY26 debt-to-equity was ~0.4x–0.45x.
Average revenue per item rose ~6% YoY and ~7% QoQ to INR 1,663; occupancy remained 85%–86%.
Cash flow from operations has exceeded EBITDA for three years; FY26 operating cash flow was ~INR 173 crore and normalized returns on capital exceeded 26%.

A June 2026 fire at the Noida warehouse destroyed inventory valued at ~2% of the gross asset base at WDV and caused a one-time INR 113.7 million loss; insurance coverage was in place, with no injuries or loss of life.
Management noted possible interest-rate increases and inflation in consumer durables and supply-chain costs; it characterized return-on-capital sensitivity to 1%–2% rate changes as limited.
Rental pricing can be adjusted with procurement costs; management said 10%–15% cost increases staggered over 18–20 months have limited sensitivity to conversion or margins.
Inventory planning depends on forecasting demand, churn, repair capacity, consumables, technician availability, and supply-chain timing, with occupancy reflecting those variables.

IPO was described as a major milestone; primary proceeds of INR 150 crore strengthened the balance sheet, with management estimating net worth above INR 450 crore by September after interim profit accruals.
Rental searches across furniture and appliances rose 2x–2.5x from 2021 to 2025; internal keyword trends were cited at ~20% growth.
FY26 platform orders totaled ~1 million items, representing ~INR 1,150 crore of estimated retail purchase displacement; Q1 FY27 orders were ~329,000 items.
Dixon supplied refrigerators and washing machines; procurement also includes brands such as Wakefit, Duroflex, Haier, and Samsung, with purchases guided by SKU-level consumer demand.
FY26 operating cash flow of ~INR 173 crore funded growth CapEx of INR 87.5 crore; management cited self-funded growth and normalized ROCE above 26%.
FY26 debt was ~INR 180–185 crore against cash of ~INR 35 crore, for net debt of ~INR 150 crore; INR 150 crore of IPO proceeds added to net worth.
Latest debt was raised at 8.95%, below the ~9.58% weighted average cost; management said borrowing dependence has declined as internal cash accruals fund investment.
FY26 gross block additions were ~INR 170 crore; inventory deployment is balanced against returns on capital and occupancy targets.
Normalization included the INR 113.7 million fire loss and INR 27.3 million deferred-tax adjustment; the deferred tax was non-cash, with no tax cash outflow in Q1 FY27.
Q4 FY26 normalization included a INR 29.3 million write-off of an old liability and a deferred-tax adjustment related to unwinding a deferred tax asset created in September.
Ind AS EBITDA is higher than IGAAP EBITDA because warehouse and experience-store rentals are recorded as right-of-use assets; PAT is broadly similar under both bases.
Q1 FY27 contracted revenue was INR 5,544 million, of which INR 4,079 million was unrecognized at quarter-end.
India’s average tenancy was cited at ~19 months, while relocations can cost INR 15,000–30,000; rental subscriptions address moving, repair, upgrade, and upfront-purchase burdens.

Management cited ~4.8 crore rental apartments, including ~3.8 crore in its target income bracket, with ~1.8 crore turning over annually; organized rental subscribers remain a small fraction of this pool.
Furniture and appliance rental searches rose 2x–2.5x from 2021 to 2025, while internal keyword growth was ~20%, supporting an expanding market and organic discovery.
EPFO job additions were cited as rising from 50 lakh annually to ~2 crore through FY26, supporting workforce mobility and rental demand.
